Qualitative findings: research and products favour inspectable assets and editable harnesses; no product documents persistent repository-derived model updates; evaluation centres on individual task outcomes; improvement claims need matched, held-out, longitudinal comparisons that separate update, selection and evaluation cases and report regressions and costs; a matched-budget study found evolved harnesses not consistently better than simple test-time search

Open problems: reproducibility, contamination and benchmark overfitting; feedback reliability, safety, tool dependence (test-passing patches with vulnerabilities, self-assigned verification); reversibility, harness bloat, specialisation (removal as first-class operation, complexity budgets); long-term memory, skill quality and coordination (negative transfer, producer-consumer gap); evaluation beyond short benchmarks. Survey caveat: curated collection and incomplete Q3 preclude conclusions about field-wide growth
